entry.question:
## Physical scenario

An aluminum cylinder 10 \, \mathrm{cm} long, with a cross-sectional area of 20 \, \mathrm{cm^2}, is used as a spacer between two steel walls. At 17.2^\circ \mathrm{C} it just slips between the walls. It warms to 22.3^\circ \mathrm{C}, assuming that the walls are perfectly rigid and a constant distance apart.

## Question

Calculate the total force it exerts on each wall.

## Answer choices

- A: A: -1.6tons

- B: B: -1.9tons

- C: C: -2.3tons

- D: D: -3.6tons

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image depicts a rectangular section of a pipe or duct with two parallel lines, representing the walls. At each end, there are diagonal lines indicating the conduit is fixed or joined to larger structures.

In the center, there is a dashed elliptical line highlighting a section of the pipe. An arrow points to this section with text labeling it as "A = 20 cm²," specifying the cross-sectional area of the segment. Below the pipe, there is a horizontal line with arrows at both ends, marking the length of the pipe section as "10 cm."

## Dataset metadata
